item.title: Stationary integral cycles asymptotic to a pair of oriented $n$-planes in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.37816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a uniqueness theorem for stationary integral $n$-cycles asymptotic to a pair of n-planes satisfying the symmetric angle condition. For the general angle condition, we obtain a classification for complete smooth embedded oriented minimal submanifolds with vanishing first de Rham cohomology that are asymptotic to a pair of $n$-planes.
item.dc:creator: Jooho Lee

item.title: The generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.37817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, including rigidity in the equality case. As a corollary, we obtain that isoperimetric regions are bounded. We prove the conjecture for Alexandrov spaces with two sided curvature bounds as well. A sharp Michael-Simon-type inequality for hypersurfaces in these spaces is also shown.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Agnoletto, M\'arcio Fabiano Da Silva, Stefano Nardulli, Reinaldo Resende

item.title: Sobolev Inequalities Relating Rough Riemannian Metrics to their Distance Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.37884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In previous papers, the first named author and E. Bryden explored Sobolev like inequalities relating the norm of a Riemmanian metric $g_1$, in terms of a background Riemannian metric $g_0$, in order to estimate the distance function $d_{g_1}$. Although $|g_1|_{g_0}$ is not the gradient of the distance function $d_{g_1}$, it was shown that a Morrey and Sobolev inequalities hold in their appropriate domains. In this paper we see that these results can be extended to the case where $g_1$ is a Rough Riemannian metric, something roughly analogous to an $L^{\infty}$ metric. We show that the proof of the Morrey and Sobolev inequality go through, with appropriate adjustments, as well as convergence results. We also adapt previous examples from the literature to the rough Riemannian metric case which show the hypotheses from the main theorems are necessary.
item.dc:creator: Brian Allen, Lisa Naples

item.title: Fisher Geometry of Circular Wrapped Normals: Completion and Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.37985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the intrinsic Fisher geometry of the two-parameter circular wrapped normal family. Although its finite parameters form a cylinder, its metric completion is a disk: adjoining the uniform law extends the Fisher metric to a positive-definite real-analytic metric. The Gaussian curvature vanishes at the added point, is positive nearby, and tends to $-1/2$ as the underlying standard deviation tends to zero. We prove that the curvature has exactly one nonuniform zero radius and exactly one critical radius, the latter a nondegenerate positive maximum. Opposite points sufficiently close to uniformity are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic through the uniform law, so their intrinsic distance is not attained inside the nonuniform family. In contrast, identifying the means of real normal distributions modulo a period retains a complete hyperbolic cylinder with an infinitely distant cusp. Wrapping strictly decreases Fisher information in every nonzero tangent direction, while the information deficit and its fixed-order derivatives are exponentially small as the standard deviation tends to zero. The curvature theorem is proved by convergent series and explicit analytic remainder estimates; numerical figures serve only as illustrations.
item.dc:creator: Hyun Chul Jang, Juna Lee, Nathan Negera, Kalea Plotnick, Antony Wang

item.title: New Explicit Examples of Mannheim Pairs in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct new explicit parametrizations of Mannheim pairs in Euclidean 3-space. Unlike the known examples in the literature, which are essentially slant helices or general helices, the curve presented here is neither a helix nor a slant helix. We provide the full Frenet apparatus, the explicit Cartesian coordinates expressed in terms of elementary functions, and the corresponding Mannheim partner curve. The construction is based on a specific choice of the angular function that governs the curve's tangent indicatrix, leading to integrable expressions.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Alan, Renato Teixeira, Thiago Mendon\c{c}a

item.title: The Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over higher dimensional Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.38124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a parabolic formulation of the Uhlenbeck gauge fixing theorem and use it to prove the maximal existence of the Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over compact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds for $n \geq 4$. We apply Moser's iteration technique \cite{Mo1} to give a new proof of the bound of the curvature. Using an idea of Hamilton on the Ricci flow \cite{Ha}, we also provide a new proof on uniform estimates of higher order derivatives. Furthermore, we investigate the blow-up of the Yang-Mills flow at the maximal existence time and improve an asymptotical result of Hong-Tian \cite{HT1}.
item.dc:creator: Jared Casey, Chak Hoi Chan, Min-Chun Hong

item.title: Uniqueness of the weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow in four dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We improve a parabolic version of Uhlenbeck's gauge fixing theorem for the Yang-Mills flow. This allows us to prove new existence of weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow having with better properties than Struwe's weak solution on four manifolds in \cite {St2}. Finally, we apply the new parabolic version of Uhlenbeck's gauge fixing theorem to solve the Struwe problem in \cite {St2} and prove uniqueness of weak solutions to the Yang-Mills flow on compact four-manifolds with initial value $A_0 \in W^{1, 2}(M)$.
item.dc:creator: Chak Hoi Chan, Min-Chun Hong

item.title: On the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.38257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Blaschke-Lebesgue problem seeks the convex body of minimal volume among all convex bodies of prescribed constant width. In this paper, we investigate the necessary conditions for volume minimizers of the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue problem via the inverse Gauss map and the inverse Weingarten transformation. We first introduce a generalized support function for hypersurfaces induced by the inverse Gauss map, characterize the Wigner caustic of constant width bodies, and accordingly construct convex bodies of constant width from prescribed functions. Building upon there results and applying the Brunn-Minkowski inequality, we establish a high-dimensional necessary condition: for almost every antipodal pair of a volume minimizer, one point is non-regular; at the other point, the minimum principal curvatures equals the reciprocal of the constant width. As an application, we provide a new proof for the two-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue theorem. Furthermore, we study the dimension-raising construction of Lachand-Robert and Oudet, and prove that every convex body produced by this construction satisfies our necessary condition. Finally, we put forward a conjecture stating that the sequence obtained by iterating this construction starting from a line segment yields minimizers for the Blaschke-Lebesgue problem for all dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Botao Duan, Deyan Zhang

item.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Geodesic Computation and Visualization of Geodesic Spheres on Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.38260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visualizing geodesic structures associated with general Riemannian metrics is a challenging problem in computational differential geometry. In this work, we present a computational framework for visualizing geodesics and geodesic spheres on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold equipped with the metric $g=\text{diag}(1,x^2,1), x>0$. The associated Christoffel symbols and curvature tensors are computed symbolically, and the resulting geodesic equations are solved using both \texttt{SciPy}'s numerical integration method and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The two solutions are compared to assess the accuracy of the neural network approximation. We further develop geodesic spike diagrams and surface visualizations to illustrate the deformation of geodesic spheres relative to their Euclidean counterparts. Intrinsic Riemannian surface area and volume are estimated numerically using the induced metric and the Riemannian volume density, respectively. For the chosen metric and a geodesic ball of radius one, the computed area and volume are approximately $0.362\%$ and $0.364\%$ smaller than the corresponding Euclidean values at the base grid resolution. A grid-refinement study is also performed to examine the sensitivity of these estimates to numerical resolution. The proposed framework demonstrates how symbolic differential geometry, numerical integration, and PINNs can be combined to investigate and visualize geometric structures associated with Riemannian metrics.
item.dc:creator: Sujit Bhattacharyya

item.title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
item.description: arXiv:2610.38376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. This paper is motivated by the work of Chi Li and Zhengyi Zhou, and makes a generalization to their result.
item.dc:creator: Hairun Wang

item.title: Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.38408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of Perelman's pseudolocality theorem for Ricci flow, which does not rely on Perelman's Harnack-type inequality. The key step is an estimate relating initial local $\mu$-entropy to pointed Nash entropy at later spacetime points. The argument also works for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian flow, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature lower bound. As a consequence, we can also prove the quantitative rigidity results concerning pointed Nash entropy due to Hein-Naber and Bamler for such geometric flows. In the appendix, we also show that the other results in Bamler's work (arXiv:2008.07093), when suitably modified, remain valid for Laplacian flow with bounded torsion. These include log-Sobolev/Poincar\'{e} inequality for conjugate heat kernel measure, heat kernel estimates, and dependence of the pointed Nash entropy on its basepoint.
item.dc:creator: Weiyong He, Longhuan Yan

item.title: Backward Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.38418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish a new estimate on the time-derivative of pointed Nash entropy and use it to give a new proof of backward pseudolocality for Ricci flow. The proof does not rely on Bamler's compactness theorem and structure theory concerning limits of Ricci flows. Our methods also work for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature.
item.dc:creator: Weiyong He, Longhuan Yan

item.title: Carnot geodesics with H\"older controls
item.description: arXiv:2610.38481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an explicit length-minimizing curve in a polynomial rank-two sub-Riemannian structure on $\R^4$. Its arclength parametrization is $C^{1,1/2}$ and is not $C^{1,\alpha}$ near an interior point for any $\alpha>1/2$. Minimality is proved by an approximate calibration chosen separately for each competitor. The example admits a minimizing lift to a rank-two Carnot group of step five. Generalizations are announced.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Cavallucci, Enrico Le Donne, Sebastiano Nicolussi Golo

item.title: Curvature-Dimension Conditions Along Discrete Refinement Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.38538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the sequence curvature--dimension condition $SCD(K,N)$ for complete refinement systems of finite metric probability spaces. The condition couples a transport action bound with entropy comparisons along a single probability section through the prescribed refinement layers. Within a bounded comparison range, we prove that midpoint comparisons on three consecutive layers characterize the condition on every fixed finite segment. If, in addition, the refinement sequence converges in the measured sense in its intrinsic bridge realization, then $SCD(K,N)$ is equivalent both to the vanishing of single-layer midpoint defects and to the entropic curvature--dimension condition $CD^{e}(K,N)$ of the limit. In the reverse direction, a $CD^{e}(K,N)$ bound on the limit yields quantitative recovery estimates that identify shrinking transport scales on which finite layers retain its second-order curvature comparison. These estimates are uniform over endpoint measures and include Dirac masses. Examples illustrate the effects of the refinement rule, the layer metrics and the reference measures.
item.dc:creator: Chen Tao

item.title: New explicit examples of Mannheim pair in $\mathbb{L}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct explicit examples of Mannheim pairs, in the classical sense, in Minkowski 3-space $\mathbb{L}^3$, one for each of the five types of such pairs. In our main examples the Mannheim curve is neither a helix nor a slant helix. For each example we give the complete Frenet apparatus of both curves of the pair and their Cartesian coordinates in terms of elementary functions. The construction writes the tangent indicatrix in angular coordinates and uses a suitable auxiliary angle function, which reduces all the relevant integrals to elementary form; it is carried out both starting from the Mannheim curve and starting from its partner. In these coordinates, we also characterize the helices and the slant helices with timelike axis. We also prove, for the five types, that a Mannheim curve is a slant helix if and only if its partner is a helix, and we give an explicit example of such a pair.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Alan, Renato Teixeira, Thiago Mendon\c{c}a

item.title: Prescribed mean curvature surfaces of Riemann minimal type
item.description: arXiv:2610.38563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct analogues of Riemann minimal examples among surfaces in the Euclidean 3-space whose mean curvature is given by a prescribed function on the unit sphere in terms of their Gauss map. Specifically, we obtain a 2-parameter family of complete, properly embedded surfaces foliated by circles and straight lines and invariant under a nontrivial translation.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Bueno

item.title: Solitons on Statistical Manifolds and Their Submanifolds
item.description:
arXiv:2610.38723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Statistical manifolds, introduced by Amari in information geometry, carry a pair of dual torsion-free connections $(
abla,
abla^{*})$ together with a Riemannian metric. In this chapter we survey the theory of \emph{statistical solitons}, that is, vector fields and constants that solve the Ricci-soliton equation simultaneously for $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$, together with the statistical analogue of almost quasi-Yamabe solitons. We discuss two principal settings: (i) statistical warped products $\R	imes_f N_2$ and $N_1	imes_f\R$ for (pseudo) Riemannian manifolds $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$, where the soliton equation constrains the warping function; and (ii) statistical submanifolds of Kenmotsu statistical manifolds, where the position of the Reeb field $\xi$ relative to the submanifold and the presence of concircular or concurrent vector fields determine the Einstein, $\eta$-Einstein or quasi-Einstein character of the submanifold. We further review the results of Blaga and Chen on gradient solitons and statistical structures, in particular the connections $
abla^{	heta}$ defined by a $1$-form, volume formulas and bounds for the Ricci tensor. We also describe Chen-type inequalities for statistical warped product submanifolds, which give the extrinsic context in which such solitons live. Key steps of the proofs, remarks on the sharpness of hypotheses, worked examples, and open problems are included.
item.dc:creator: Aliya Naaz Siddiqui, Bang-Yen Chen

item.title: Mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2610.38929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the arrival time equation of the mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group. We prove existence of viscosity solutions when the initial set is horizontally mean-convex and either non-characteristic, or axisymmetric and with horizontal mean curvature extending continuously across the characteristic set. A key ingredient is an approximation scheme by sets with prescribed Riemannian mean curvature, which preserves the mean-curvature bounds up to an arbitrarily small error. We further show that, when the evolving level sets form a generalized \(C^2\)-foliation, the horizontal mean curvature blows up around characteristic points. This provides an obstruction to self-similar evolution in the axisymmetric class considered above and, in particular, shows that the Pansu sphere cannot evolve self-similarly.
item.dc:creator: Gaia Bombardieri, Mattia Fogagnolo, Valentina Franceschi

item.title: Compactification of parabolic Hermitian--Einstein moduli spaces on complex surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.38958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\overline{X}$ be a compact complex surface with a Gauduchon metric, and let $D\subset\overline{X}$ be a smooth connected divisor. We construct an Uhlenbeck compactification of the moduli space of rank-two parabolic Hermitian--Einstein connections with prescribed holomorphic determinant.
item.dc:creator: Xilun Li, Gang Tian

item.title: Topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.38962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition on length-minimizing curves in the metric tangent space. We prove that sufficiently small spheres are Lipschitz hypersurfaces homeomorphic to Euclidean spheres, while closed balls are homeomorphic to Euclidean closed balls, and open balls are diffeomorphic to Euclidean open balls. These results improve the known ones and extend them beyond two-step distributions. The proof relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for the distance, of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Luca Rizzi, Giuditta Rovelli

item.title: The cross quadratic bisectional curvature of K\"{a}hler $C$-spaces of classical type
item.description: arXiv:2610.39012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that any K\"{a}hler $C$-space of classical type has nonnegative cross quadratic bisectional curvature and positive dual cross quadratic bisectional curvature. As a consequence, such manifolds are Fano. This confirms a substantial part of a conjecture of Ni-Zheng (Conjecture 1.5 in \cite{NZ}).
item.dc:creator: Run-Qiang Jian, Zhuhong Zhang

item.title: Synge's Theorem and a Sphere Theorem in Weighted Intermediate Ricci Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.39015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the tools developed by Kennard, Wylie, and Yeroshkin for weighted sectional curvature bounds, we generalize a theorem of Wilhelm to show that Synge's Theorem holds for manifolds with density that have positive weighted intermediate Ricci curvature and a sufficiently large first systole. Furthermore, we provide a sphere theorem for compact manifolds with positive weighted intermediate Ricci curvature.
item.dc:creator: Hasan M. El-Hasan, Curtis Pro

item.title: Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics on nilpotent Lie groups and the quasicentroid condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.39184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study left-invariant Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics (cyclic-parallel Ricci tensor) on nilpotent Lie groups, focusing on the algebraic condition that the Ricci operator belongs to the quasicentroid $\operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}$. We review and develop the abstract structure theory of quasicentroids, and prove a Central Decomposition Theorem: any nilpotent Riemannian Lie algebra with $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ decomposes as a central product of ideals $\mathfrak{i}_j = E_{\lambda_j} \oplus \mathfrak{z}$, where $\mathfrak{z}$ is the center of $\mathfrak{n}$ and $E_{\lambda_j}$ are the negative Ricci eigenspaces. Endowed with the restricted metric, each factor $\mathfrak{i}_j$ is itself a Gray $\mathcal{A}$-space. Finally, we investigate when the general $\mathcal{A}$-metric condition reduces to $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$. We prove this equivalence unconditionally for two-step nilpotent algebras and whenever the metric admits a nice basis, and provide a general characterization via the vanishing of two trace identities.
item.dc:creator: Edison Alberto Fern\'{a}ndez-Culma

item.title: Dually flat structure of von Mises-Fisher distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.39249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The von Mises--Fisher (vMF) distribution is the natural exponential family analogue of the normal distribution on the unit hypersphere. We bring together previous results of its dually flat structure and establish new results on the information geometry of the family of vMF distributions. In particular, we characterize the exponential and mixture autoparallel submanifolds, and give the classification of doubly autoparallel submanifolds. Furthermore, we derive explicit formulas for the unique minimizers of the Kullback-Leibler divergence on these submanifolds and establish the corresponding projection theorems.
item.dc:creator: Behzad Najafi, Morteza Sharifi-Najjar, Ryu Ueno

item.title: On the geometry of asymptotically conical Ricci shrinkers (I): weighted analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.39814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the weighted Sobolev and H\"older analysis needed to study perturbations of complete asymptotically conical (AC) Ricci shrinkers. Weighted elliptic estimates yield a global weighted divergence-free slice in spaces that retain the asymptotic data at infinity. As a geometric application, we prove pointed Gromov-Hausdorff rigidity of nontrivial AC shrinkers with vanishing infinitesimal solitonic deformation space.
item.dc:creator: Yu Li, Longhuan Yan, Wenjia Zhang

item.title: Planarity estimates and codimension reduction for ancient flows at the Andrews-Baker threshold
item.description: arXiv:2610.39877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an interior planarity estimate for space-time proper mean curvature flows of $n$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb R^{n+p}$, $n\geq5$, that are uniformly quadratically pinched up to the Andrews-Baker threshold $\frac{4}{3n}$. The estimate is parabolically scale-invariant and it requires neither curvature nor entropy bounds. The proof combines Naff's gradient estimates with a localization argument in the spirit of Ecker and Huisken. In dimensions five and six, Naff's estimates alone do not give the gradient terms a sign. We bound these terms from below with an argument we developed in a previous work. As a consequence, for $n\geq5$, and by known results for $2\leq n\leq4$, every space-time proper ancient solution that is uniformly $\frac{4}{3n}$-pinched is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-dimensional subspace. This replaces the finite entropy and polynomial curvature growth assumptions of Lee, Naff and Zhu by space-time properness, and improves their pinching constant in dimensions two, five and six. For closed flows, we extend Lynch's planarity estimate to a larger range of exponents.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Ruatta

item.title: A New Invariant for Doubly Periodic Solutions of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. These transcendental period conditions are studied through Whitham deformations, which deform the curve while preserving the periods. We extend Whitham deformations to all real hyperelliptic curves of this type, by holding fixed the plane spanned by the periods, or this plane together with its complex structure. Under mild nondegeneracy conditions the resulting isoperiodic sets are manifolds of dimensions three and one, respectively. Along the one-dimensional isoperiodic sets, a generalization of the Willmore energy is a local parameter away from its critical points, to which the spectral curves of tori belong. Finally, using homology bases adapted to the branch points, we find discrete invariants of the isoperiodic sets of doubly periodic curves: a triple of integers and a refined conformal type.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Hasse, Ross Ogilvie, Martin U. Schmidt

item.title: Three-dimensional noncompact trans-Sasakian $\eta$-Einstein manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.39971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify connected, simply connected, noncompact three-dimensional trans-Sasakian $\eta$-Einstein manifolds. In [1], we showed that, in the compact case, such a manifold is either of $\beta$-Kenmotsu type or homothetic to a Sasakian manifold. In this paper, in the noncompact case, we find families of trans-Sasakian $\eta$-Einstein manifolds that are neither $\beta$-Kenmotsu nor homothetic to Sasakian manifolds. These families have infinitely many degrees of freedom. We give these nontrivial metrics explicitly. We also give a structure theorem for the case in which the characteristic vector field is Palais-nonregular.
item.dc:creator: Satsuki Matsuno

item.title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for weighted curvature integrals in space forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.40087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish two types of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for the weighted curvature integrals of static convex domains in space forms. The first type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving three weighted curvature integrals, with the second Minkowski type inequality of Xia [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 55 (2016), Art. 96] and the weighted almost Schur lemma of Li and Xia [J. Differential Geom. 113 (2019), pp. 493--518] as special cases. The second type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving two weighted curvature integrals, confirming a conjectured geometric inequality by Hu and Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 375 (2022), pp. 5587--5615]. The key novelty lies in observing that, via the orthogonal projection map, the weighted curvature integrals for domains in space forms admit a natural interpretation in terms of mixed volumes of Euclidean convex bodies, thus reducing the problem to the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in convex geometry.
item.dc:creator: Botong Xu

item.title: Hypersurface and Foliation Isoparametric Transfer for Generalized $(\alpha,\beta)$-Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.40128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F=\alpha\Phi(q,s)$ be a regular generalized $(\alpha,\beta)$-metric, where $q=\|\beta\|_\alpha^2$ and $s=\beta/\alpha$, endowed with the Busemann--Hausdorff or Holmes--Thompson volume. We derive explicit comparison formulas for the induced hypersurface volume and the associated volume mean curvature and use them to study two transfer problems suggested by the Randers case. The first asks whether the same hypersurface is isoparametric for $\alpha$ and $F$; the second asks whether the same regular foliation is isoparametric for both metrics. Exact local and global criteria are obtained. Their Randers specializations recover the corresponding hypersurface transfer and the condition $df(W)=\varphi(f)$. We also prove an all-normal induced-volume rigidity theorem and construct a complete non-Randers example realizing both transfer mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Yali Chen

item.title: Whitham Deformations of Nodal Spectral Curves of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.40197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. Deformations that preserve the periods, called Whitham deformations, are well understood for nonsingular curves, where the isoperiodic sets are manifolds. We extend Whitham deformations to curves with ordinary double points that are fixed by the real involution. At such curves the isoperiodic sets remain manifolds and are transverse to the curves with double points, so Whitham deformations can change the genus of the spectral curve. We describe how the double points open, and when the derivative of the normalized Willmore energy vanishes at a nodal curve. By inserting double points, we show that every value of a discrete invariant of the isoperiodic sets found in previous work occurs.
item.dc:creator: Ross Ogilvie

item.title: Levi-Civita's type theorem for projectively equivalent sub-Riemannian metrics on step 2 distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper extends the classical results of Eisenhart (1923) and Levi-Civita (1896) on the classification of pairs of germs of Riemannian metrics with the same geodesics, either as parametrized curves (affine equivalence) or as unparametrized curves (projective equivalence), to sub-Riemannian metrics on arbitrary step 2 distributions: at every stable point in the projective case and at every point in the affine case. This extends the results of Zelenko (2004) for contact and even-contact distributions and the affine result of Lin and Zelenko (2024) for step 2 distributions with ad-surjective Tanaka symbols; our projective result covers the ad-surjective case as well. In the affine case, we prove that if a sub-Riemannian metric admits an affinely equivalent metric that is not constantly proportional to it, then locally it is a product of two sub-Riemannian metrics. In the projective case, we prove the 2019 conjecture of Jean, Maslovskaya, and Zelenko on generalized Levi-Civita pairs; in particular, the distribution admits a product structure, the squares of its components are involutive, and the restrictions of the two metrics to each leaf of the corresponding foliation are conformal to each other under the appropriate pullback. The proof is based on a new graph-theoretic formalism, in which compatible moving frames are represented by the vertices and edges of certain graphs. As a byproduct, we introduce a new discrete invariant of step 2 nilpotent graded Lie algebras, the characteristic tuple. The compatible graphs are used on the open dense set where this tuple is locally constant; the resulting bracket relations are identities between smooth tensors, so they extend by continuity across the points where the tuple jumps. Consequently, our classification holds without any assumption of local constancy of the characteristic tuple.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sinkule, Igor Zelenko

item.title: Ricci curvature of semigroup walks on graphs and generator representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.40301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an operator-theoretic framework for the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of (one-parameter families of) random walks generated by positive semigroups on graphs. On a metrically complete graph $(G,d)$ that is $d$-locally finite, we introduce a class of admissible semigroup random walks whose infinitesimal first-order approximation is itself a random walk. We prove that the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of an admissible semigroup random walk is well-defined and completely determined by its first-order approximation. We then establish a variational representation of the curvature of random walks in terms of a notion of the initial-time generator. This representation applies in particular to admissible semigroup random walks. Finally, we use this representation to define an operator-theoretic Ollivier--Ricci curvature for operators acting on spaces of functions over general metric spaces and establish sufficient conditions for well-definedness. This framework contains, in particular, Markovian random walks associated with discrete Laplacians.
item.dc:creator: Sajjad Lakzian

item.title: Complete K\"ahler Manifolds with pinched Ricci curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.40419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that a connected complete K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension at least two satisfying $\Ric\geq\varepsilon Rg\geq0$ for a fixed $\varepsilon>0$ is compact or Ricci-flat.
item.dc:creator: Yuxing Deng, Ruyi Ji

item.title: Willmore inequalities beyond the injectivity radius
item.description: arXiv:2610.40546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize a method first introduced by Li, Yau, Simon, and Topping (for closed surfaces immersed in the flat Euclidean space), and we establish a global-in-nature estimate, with an explicit cut-locus contribution, on the Willmore energy of closed surfaces that are immersed in a complete Riemannian three-manifold and need not be embedded. Our estimate applies to ambient spaces whose sectional curvature is bounded above and whose injectivity radius may be finite. For positive upper curvature bounds, the global weighted estimates require an explicit radius restriction. The Willmore energy is bounded below by a functional involving the self-intersection number of the surface and the injectivity radius of the ambient space. Furthermore, by investigating in what sense our inequalities are optimal and realized by geodesic spheres in constant curvature spaces, we are led to introduce a weighted version of the Willmore functional, which is adapted to geodesic spheres in the model spaces and takes the sectional curvature of the ambient space into account. As a corollary, we obtain sufficient conditions for an immersed surface in a curved space to be embedded.
item.dc:creator: Philippe G. LeFloch

item.title: Some remarks on robust features of surfaces in 4-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.40604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study robust features of smooth surfaces in 4-space associated with contact with lines and hyperplanes. We investigate the local and multi-local singularities of orthogonal projections and height functions that describe these contacts and their corresponding geometric loci on the surface. At an $A_4$-singularity of a height function, we show that the $A_3$-curve and the $A_1A_2$-curve are generically tangent with contact of order $2$. We further establish criteria for the versality of the families of height functions and orthogonal projections in terms of the regularity of the $B_2$-curve and $S_2$-curve, respectively. Finally, we obtain the $[A_2]$- and $(A_0S_0)_2$-curves arising from multi-local singularities of orthogonal projections and describe their tangency properties at the $B_3$- and $H_3$-singularities.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Luiz Deolindo-Silva

item.title: An $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling inequality in every dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.37886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\geq2$) be measurable with $0<|\Omega|<\infty$, and let $u_\Omega$ be its logarithmic potential ($N=2$) or Newtonian potential ($N\geq3$), normalized so that $\Delta u_\Omega=\chi_\Omega$. We prove the sharp inequality \[ \int_\Omega|\nabla u_\Omega|^2\,\mathrm{d} x \leq\frac{1}{2N\omega_{N-1}} \iint_{\Omega\times\Omega}\frac{\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} y}{|x-y|^{N-2}}, \] where $\omega_{N-1}=|\mathbb{S}^{N-1}|$, with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is a ball up to a null set. In dimension two this settles the $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling conjecture of Fleeman and Khavinson. For $N\ge3$ it is equivalent to the scale-free bound that at most the fraction $(N-2)/(2N)$ of the total field energy lies inside $\Omega$. We also obtain an explicit deficit identity, a sharp extension to bounded nonnegative densities, and consequences for torsional rigidity, Bergman analytic content, Brownian motion, and aggregation equations.
item.dc:creator: Guofang Wang, Mingwei Zhang

item.title: Calabi-Yau Hyperbolicity
item.description: arXiv:2610.37996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The goal of this paper is to introduce a new notion of hyperbolicity for compact complex manifolds with trivial canonical bundle, called \textit{Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity}. We investigate its fundamental properties and establish a characterization in terms of the fundamental group. In particular, we show that no compact K\"ahler Calabi--Yau manifold is Calabi--Yau hyperbolic, highlighting the genuinely non-K\"ahler nature of this notion. We also investigate different techniques for constructing examples of such manifolds. Finally, we examine the relationship between Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity and Kobayashi hyperbolicity in the examples considered, highlighting obstructions to the latter in the Calabi--Yau setting.
item.dc:creator: Abdelouahab Khelifati

item.title: Graph-diameter criteria and sharp dissipation in discrete Wasserstein-Fisher geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.38129v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the probability simplex of a finite connected weighted graph with an Onsager operator combining logarithmic-mean transport and mass-conserving Fisher reaction. For every fixed positive reaction parameter, we prove that the entropy Hessian has a finite global lower bound if and only if the original transport graph has diameter at most two. Near a boundary probability, the corresponding criterion is that its positive support reaches every vertex in at most two steps. The proof controls all potential directions under arbitrary multiscale boundary degeneration. For graphs of diameter at most two, the optimal lower bound is Lipschitz on bounded parameter intervals, including the pure-transport endpoint. We also determine the largest instantaneous logarithmic-amplitude dissipation function depending only on the graph and the current amplitude, and construct two-level probabilities attaining it. Its positivity has the same two-step criterion. As consequences, we obtain graph-dependent entropy-decay estimates and exact projective contraction bounds without assuming nonnegative entropic curvature.
item.dc:creator: Rubin Zhang, Ning Zhang

item.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties II -soliton case-
item.description: arXiv:2610.38137v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by recent work of Inoue and Hallam-Lahdili, we prove an equivariant Miyaoka-Yau inequality with a correction term for smooth Fano manifolds admitting K\"ahler-Ricci solitons. It recovers the usual Miyaoka-Yau inequality in the K\"ahler-Einstein case. Our proof uses weighted equivariant Bogomolov-Gieseker and Langer inequalities for torsion-free sheaves, together with a weighted slope estimate for the canonical extension sheaf. We also construct toric examples showing that the existence of a soliton implies neither weighted semistability of the canonical extension sheaf nor nonnegativity of the equivariant Miyaoka-Yau number.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Hisamoto, Masataka Iwai

item.title: Einstein Metrics and Quantum Control on Symmetric Tensor Product Quotients
item.description: arXiv:2610.38340v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M_n=(\mathrm{PU}(2)^n\rtimes S_n)\backslash\mathrm{PU}(2^n)$ be the space of projective $n$-qubit unitaries modulo local unitaries and permutations of the qubits. We prove that for all sufficiently large $n$ the manifold $M_n$ carries exactly two $\mathrm{PU}(2^n)$-invariant Einstein metrics up to scaling. Both Einstein metrics have uniformly bounded diameter after normalizing two-qubit costs, although approximating a Haar-random unitary requires exponentially many two-qubit gates. In contrast, we construct non-Einstein metrics with nonnegative Ricci curvature and exponentially growing typical control distances, and determine the sharp curvature threshold for this family.
item.dc:creator: Honghuai Fang

item.title: The geometry of Floquet states
item.description: arXiv:2610.38845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians. The paper also considers the adiabatic driving of a 1-parameter family of good periodic Hamiltonians. We formulate two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution. These are Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem in quantum mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Y. Cherynak, John R. Klein

item.title: Analysis of blowup masses in constant-coefficient Toda systems: W-invariants and Weyl orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.38905v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the local blowup masses of constant-coefficient Toda systems for all simple Lie algebras with one prescribed singular source, bounded component masses, and bounded boundary oscillations. We encode the source strengths and the blowup masses by two elements of the Cartan subalgebra: the grading element $p_\mu$ and the mass element $q_\sigma$. We show that $p_\mu-q_\sigma=wp_\mu$ for some Weyl group element $w\in W$. The proof uses the Drinfeld-Sokolov gauge and the resulting holomorphic $W$-invariants for Toda systems. Asymptotic analysis near the source and on a shrinking circle enclosing the total local mass gives two evaluations of the leading Laurent coefficients of the $W$-invariants, which agree by holomorphicity. This agreement enables us to conclude the above Weyl-orbit result. In particular, the quadratic constraint is the local Pohozaev identity. Only with the full set of $W$-invariants can we strengthen earlier orbit-plus-integer restrictions to an exact Weyl-orbit characterization in the constant-coefficient setting. Together with the author's explicit families in [Nie], this determines all attainable local mass vectors.
item.dc:creator: Zhaohu Nie

item.title: Logarithmic transformations on the six-sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.39102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that there are infinitely many choices of the multiplicities in the logarithmic transformation step of the Alp\"oge--Claude construction which produce a complex threefold diffeomorphic to the six-sphere. Moreover, distinct choices of the multiplicities yield biholomorphically inequivalent complex structures.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Viaclovsky

item.title: Minimally-coupled Quasilinear Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems, Naturally
item.description: arXiv:2610.39107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider symmetric hyperbolicity and well-posedness in the context of natural equations, which are closed subobjects of jet bundles over natural bundles. We show how non-natural equations can be "naturalized", and we discuss how a precise version of "minimal coupling" offers a (provably unique, up to isomorphism) method for constructing natural equations from certain equations defined on a single manifold. We discuss how to define symmetrizers, hyperbolizations, and constraints for minimally coupled natural equations, and we show how these can be used to recover standard existence and uniqueness results, relative to any choice of background structure (a metric, for minimally coupled systems). Additionally, we show that minimal coupling and naturality together imply that the causal cones associated with a (first order, quasilinear, minimally coupled) naturally symmetric hyperbolic natural equation must always coincide with the metric lightcones, and that a certain rank-2 tensor, associates with a natural hyperbolization, must always be divergence free relative to the associated Levi-Civita derivative operator.
item.dc:creator: Eleanor March, James Owen Weatherall

item.title: Uniform estimates for complex Monge-Amp\`ere equations II: Hermitian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.39259v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish uniform estimates for degenerate complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations on compact Hermitian manifolds under weak Orlicz integrability assumptions on the densities. Our estimates apply uniformly to Hermitian metrics and to semipositive uniformly non-collapsing reference forms. For arbitrary big reference forms, we obtain uniform relative $L^\infty$-estimates with respect to the extremal function with minimal singularities, and establish continuity of the resulting solutions on the regular locus. As an application, we prove the existence of solutions with minimal singularities to degenerate complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations associated with big forms. The proofs combine local Orlicz estimates with pluripotential-theoretic envelope techniques and uniform control of the Monge--Amp\`ere masses, overcoming the lack of invariance of the total Monge--Amp\`ere mass in the Hermitian setting.
item.dc:creator: Quang-Tuan Dang, Lei Zhang, Bin Zhou

item.title: Lipschitz volume rigidity for non-collapsed $\rm RCD$ spaces with boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.39493v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Lipschitz-volume rigidity for non-collapsed ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces, possibly with boundary. We prove that a measure-preserving $1$-Lipschitz map between such spaces restricts to an isometry from the interior of the domain onto its image, where the latter is equipped with the intrinsic length distance. We then characterize when this interior rigidity extends to an isometric bijection between the whole spaces, in terms of the behavior of the map on the boundaries. Along the way, we establish a rigidity result of independent interest in a more general class of rectifiable metric spaces.
item.dc:creator: Zhenhao Li, Enrico Pasqualetto, Xin Qian

item.title: Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps from $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces to $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for local Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps in the sense of Korevaar and Schoen from finite-dimensional \(\RCD(K,N)\) spaces into complete \(\CAT(0)\) spaces, without assuming harmonicity. We quantify the failure of local energy minimality by the harmonic replacement potential, a dyadic sum of the square roots of normalized energy gaps between a map and its harmonic replacements. We prove that this potential, together with an averaged energy term, controls the minimal weak upper gradient pointwise, with constants depending only on the curvature-dimension bounds and the scale. In particular, local boundedness of the replacement potential implies that the map admits a locally Lipschitz representative.
item.dc:creator: Bang-Xian Han, Zeyu Wang

item.title: A new sharp Sobolev inequality between the $Q$-curvature and the scalar curvature on Euclidean space
item.description: arXiv:2610.39659v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a sharp Sobolev-type inequality on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 5$, that interpolates between the second-order energy and a weighted first-order term. Specifically, we determine the sharp constant $S_{4,2}$ in the inequality \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^n} (\Delta u)^2\,dx \ge S_{4,2} \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\nabla u|^{2}|u|^{\frac{4}{n-4}}\,dx\right)^{\frac{n-4}{n-2}}, \end{equation*} for any $u\in\dot H^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and we classify the cases of equality. This solves the problem of minimizing the total $Q$-curvature of among metrics on the sphere, conformal to the standard metric, with fixed total scalar curvature.
item.dc:creator: Rupert L. Frank, Yuxin Ge, Guofang Wang, Wei Wei

item.title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vign\'eras
item.description: arXiv:2610.39874v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. This is a converse to the construction of Vign\'eras, which produces isospectral manifolds from maximal orders of different types. In particular the spectral genus of $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ has at most $t(B)$ elements, and $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is spectrally rigid when the type number $t(B)$ is one. In dimension three we prove the same statements for manifolds that, in addition, have the same complex lengths of closed geodesics. The proof rests on a local result that characterizes, by traces alone, the subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}(2)$ over a $p$-adic ring that are conjugate into a principal congruence subgroup by traces. As applications, every principal congruence Hurwitz surface is spectrally rigid, among them Klein's quartic, the Fricke-Macbeath surface and the surfaces of the first Hurwitz triplet, which partially answers a question of Reid.
item.dc:creator: Justin Katz, D. B. McReynolds

item.title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.
item.dc:creator: Milan Pavlovi\'{c}, Tijana \v{S}ukilovi\'{c}

item.title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40076v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Del Donno

item.title: A complete solution to the reverse isoperimetric problem for $\lambda$-convex bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.40291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a given $\lambda > 0$, a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $\lambda$-convex if it is the intersection of balls of radius $1/\lambda$. We show that among all $\lambda$-convex bodies in $\mathbb R^n$ of a given surface area, volume is minimized by the $\lambda$-convex lens, that is, the intersection of two balls of radius $1/\lambda$. This confirms a conjecture of Borisenko in all dimensions $n \geq 2$. Moreover, we extend this reverse isoperimetric inequality to all model spaces of constant curvature in arbitrary dimension and arbitrary $\lambda > 0$.
item.dc:creator: Kostiantyn Drach, Kateryna Tatarko

item.title: Localization in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.40514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Seven-dimensional supergravity provides holographic access to strongly coupled six-dimensional superconformal theories through its highest-dimensional supersymmetric AdS vacua. Its unique spinor-bilinear geometry and massive higher-form dynamics make systematic analysis and solution-finding distinctively challenging. Relative equivariant localization can obtain supersymmetric observables in odd dimensions from fixed-point data on an auxiliary even-dimensional filling, without an explicit solution. We extend this approach to seven dimensions in maximal Cartan-gauged supergravity with all gauge fields active. We formulate the Euclidean action and Killing-spinor equations in terms of field strengths, and construct a bilinear system adapted to the change in spinor reality conditions from symplectic-Majorana to Majorana. On the non-null gauged active spinor branch, independent, oppositely R-charged spinors are paired by Majorana conjugation on the same complex background. One algebraic gauging correction and two algebraic bilinear projections suffice to extend the equal-charge sector to independent Cartan charges, and the underlying efficient reorganization also applies in the Lorentzian theory. Massive 3-form self-duality fixes the quartic anomaly class and determines the higher-form fixed-point datum from Abelian moment maps. Localization at the single fixed point of the filling recovers the general supersymmetric AdS$_7$ black-hole action, without extending the solution. We prove gauge-covariant Killing-spinor invariance under the combined supersymmetric Killing flow and R-symmetry action, deriving the linear chemical-potential constraint. Extremizing the constrained entropy functional and requiring real positive stationary entropy yields the nonlinear charge relation within the Euclidean analysis, equivalent to Lorentzian horizon extremality for the known spherical black-hole family.
item.dc:creator: Florian Gaar, Mich\`ele Levi

item.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.40639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that all compact hyperk\"ahler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojevi\'c and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact K\"ahler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Pio Contr\`o

item.title: Non-collapsing of fibers in warped-product Poincare--Einstein manifolds
item.description: arXiv:0710.2699v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $g=g_M+u^2h$ be a Poincar\'e--Einstein (asymptotically hyperbolic Einstein, AHE) metric of class $C^{3,\alpha}$ on $N^{n+1}=M^q\times F^p$, where $(F,h)$ is compact with unit volume and $\Ric_h=\lambda h$, $\lambda\le 0$. We show that if the conformal infinity $[\gamma]$ has positive Yamabe constant, then \[ u\;\ge\;\Theta[\gamma]:=\sup_{\eta}\Big(\min_{\dN}\psi_\eta\Big)\Big(\frac{\min_{\dN} s_\eta}{n(n-1)}\Big)^{1/2}>0, \] the supremum being over representatives $\eta\in[\gamma]$ of positive scalar curvature and $\psi_\eta$ the boundary warping function of $\eta$. In particular $u\ge (\Y[\gamma]/n(n-1))^{1/2}\min\psi_{\eta_Y}$ for the Yamabe metric $\eta_Y$. The estimate rests on a comparison principle between $\ln u$ and Lee's eigenfunction, which also applies to each factor of a multiply warped product, and pointwise yields $u\ge(\min\psi_\eta)\,w_\eta$ when $\Y[\gamma]\ge 0$. We give an explicit bound in terms of the product representative of $[\gamma]$, show that the hypotheses force $q\ge 3$ and $\partial M$ connected, prove lower semicontinuity of $\Theta$ in the boundary data, and discuss examples (hyperbolic Fermi coordinates, AdS--Schwarzschild) showing that the hypothesis $\lambda\le0$ cannot be removed.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: A generalization of the Perelman gluing theorem and applications
item.description: arXiv:2308.06996v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend a positive Ricci curvature gluing theorem of Perelman to a range of positive intermediate curvature conditions, ranging from positive scalar curvature up to (and including) positive sectional curvature. As an application of this, we demonstrate that the observer moduli space of metrics with positive intermediate Ricci curvatures can have non-trivial higher homotopy groups. Further applications include deriving a sufficient condition for the existence of a metric with positive intermediate Ricci curvature and totally geodesic boundary.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Reiser, David J. Wraith

item.title: The Einstein-Hilbert functional and the Donaldson-Futaki invariant
item.description: arXiv:2310.11625v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a Kaehler manifold polarised by a holomorphic ample line bundle, we consider the circle bundle associated to the polarisation with the induced transversal holomorphic structure. The space of contact structures compatible with this transversal structure is naturally identified with a bundle, of infinite rank, over the space of Kaehler metrics in the first Chern class of the polarisation. We show that the Einstein-Hilbert functional of the associated Tanaka-Webster connections is a functional on this bundle, whose critical points are constant scalar curvature Sasaki structures. In particular, when the group of automorphisms is discrete, these critical points correspond to constant scalar curvature Kaehler metrics in the first Chern class of the polarisation. We show that the Einstein--Hilbert functional satisfies some monotonicity properties along some one-parameter families of CR-contact structures that are naturally associated to test configurations, and that its limit on the central fibre of a test configuration is related to the Donaldson-Futaki invariant through an expansion in terms of an extra real parameter. As a by-product, we obtain an original proof that the existence of constant scalar curvature Kaehler metrics on a polarized manifold implies K-semistability. We also show that the limit of the Einstein-Hilbert functional on the central fibre coincides with the ratio of the equivariant index characters pole coefficients of the central fibre.
item.dc:creator: Abdellah Lahdili, Eveline Legendre, Carlo Scarpa

item.title: Covariant derivatives in the representation-valued Bott-Shulman-Stasheff and Weil complex
item.description:
arXiv:2503.08873v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a Lie groupoid $G$, the differential forms on its nerve comprise a double complex. A natural question is if this statement extends to forms with values in a representation $V$ of $G$. In this paper, we research two types of covariant derivatives which commute with the simplicial differential, yielding two types of curved double complexes of forms with coefficients in $V$. The naive approach is to consider a linear connection $
abla$ on $V$, in which case $d^
abla$ commutes with the simplicial differential if and only if $
abla$ satisfies a certain (restrictive) invariance condition. The heart of this paper focuses on another, more compelling approach: using a multiplicative Ehresmann connection for a bundle of ideals. In this case, we obtain a geometrically richer curved double complex, where the cochain map is given by the horizontal exterior covariant derivative $D$, which generalizes the well-known operator from the theory of principal bundles. Moreover, both differential operators $d^
abla$ and $D$ are researched in the infinitesimal setting of Lie algebroids, as well as their relationship with the van Est map. We conclude by using the operator $D$ to study the curvature of an (infinitesimal) multiplicative Ehresmann connection.
item.dc:creator: \v{Z}an Grad

item.title: The Willmore Energy Landscape of Spheres and Avoidable Singularities of the Willmore Flow
item.description: arXiv:2506.23359v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the sublevel sets of the Willmore energy on the space of smoothly immersed $ 2 $-spheres in Euclidean $ 3 $-space. We show that the subset of immersions with energy at most $ 12\pi $ consists of four regular homotopy classes. Moreover, we show that in certain regular homotopy classes, all singularities of the Willmore flow are avoidable, that is, the initial surface admits a regular homotopy to a round sphere whose Willmore energy does not exceed that of the initial surface. This yields a classification of initial surfaces with energy at most $ 12\pi $ that lead to unavoidable singularities. As a further consequence, we obtain an extension of the Li-Yau inequality at $ 12\pi $ for a large class of immersed spheres without triple points. To prove these results, we glue together different instances of the Willmore flow and employ an invariant for triple-point-free immersed spheres.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M\"ader-Baumdicker, E. and Seidel, J. (2026) 'The Willmore Energy Landscape of Spheres and Avoidable Singularities of the Willmore Flow', Forum of Mathematics, Sigma, 14, p. e134
item.dc:creator: Elena M\"ader-Baumdicker, Jona Seidel

item.title: Integral Points and Volume of Integral-Integral Affine Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2508.17551v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using rational Ehrhart theory and Fourier analysis, we give an elementary proof that the volume of a closed manifold equipped with an integral-integral affine structure equals the number of its integral points.
item.dc:creator: Oded Elisha, Yael Karshon, Yiannis Loizides

item.title: K\"ahler-Einstein toric submanifolds of the projective space
item.description: arXiv:2512.03617v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the K\"ahler-Einstein metrics on the four families of symmetric toric Fano manifolds due to Batyrev and Selivanova cannot be induced by immersions into projective spaces equipped with the Fubini-Study metric. We also show a similar conclusion for the non-symmetric examples discovered by Nill and Paffenholz. As an application we obtain that a centrally symmetric toric Fano manifold admits a K\"ahler-Einstein metric induced by a projective immersion if and only if it is a product of projective lines. These results confirm for each of these examples a broader conjecture characterizing the K\"ahler--Einstein metrics that can be induced by projective immersions.
item.dc:creator: Antonio J. Di Scala, Mart\'in Sombra

item.title: Reducible Holonomy in Closed Torsion Geometries
item.description: arXiv:2602.01458v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The purpose of this note is to show that a connection with closed skew-symmetric torsion and reducible holonomy admits a locally defined Riemannian submersion together with a projected geometry on the base. We reframe known submersion results for non-K\"ahler Bismut-Hermite-Einstein manifolds and sHKT structures in this context. For homogeneous SKT structures on semi-simple Lie groups, we obtain the holonomy decomposition leading to holomorphic submersions over generalized flag manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Leander Stecker

item.title: Gel'fand's inverse problem under Ricci curvature bounds
item.description: arXiv:2602.14527v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical Gel'fand's inverse problem asks whether a Riemannian manifold is uniquely determined by the knowledge of the heat kernel on any open subset of the manifold. We study this inverse problem in the non-smooth setting in the framework of ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces, namely, metric-measure spaces with synthetic Riemannian Ricci curvature bounded below by $K$ and dimension bounded above by $N$. We establish the unique solvability of Gel'fand's inverse problem for the class of compact ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces whose regular set admits Lipschitz Riemannian structure. As an application, we obtain the continuity of Gel'fand's inverse problem in the class of closed Riemannian manifolds with bounded Ricci curvature, diameter and volume bounded from below. We note that the results are new even for Einstein orbifolds and (weighted) Lipschitz Riemannian manifolds with non-smooth boundary.
item.dc:creator: Shouhei Honda, Jinpeng Lu

item.title: Distance Functions, Curvature and Topology
item.description: arXiv:2602.17629v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss some properties of the distance functions on Riemannian manifolds and we relate their behavior to the geometry of the manifolds. This leads to alternative proofs of some "classical" theorems connecting curvature and topology.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Mantegazza, Francesca Oronzio

item.title: Mass-type invariants in the presence of a cosmological constant
item.description: arXiv:2603.01543v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new family of mass-type invariants for time-symmetric initial data in space-times satisfying the Dominant Energy Condition. For positive cosmological constant, these invariants, unlike the total Hawking mass, turn out to be genuinely effective in providing new characterizations of the de Sitter solution. From a theoretical standpoint, this opens a new perspective on how one might refine the rigidity statement originally proposed by Min-Oo in his well known conjecture, later refuted by the counterexamples of Brendle, Marques, and Neves. Via a formal limiting procedure, we also define another invariant, the 1-harmonic Mass, for which we independently prove a positive mass theorem and a Penrose-type inequality, thereby extending tools for probing space-time geometries in the presence of a positive cosmological constant.
item.dc:creator: Virginia Agostiniani, Stefano Borghini, Lorenzo Mazzieri

item.title: Area and antipodal distance in convex hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.02667v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a lower bound for the surface area of a closed, convex hypersurface in Euclidean space in terms of its displacement under continuous maps. As a result, a hypothesized lower bound for the volume of a Riemannian $n$-sphere, proved by Berger in dimension $n=2$ and disproved by Croke in dimensions $n \geq 3$, is valid for convex hypersurfaces in all dimensions. We also establish a sharp lower bound for the mean width of a convex hypersurface.
item.dc:creator: James Dibble, Joseph Ansel Hoisington

item.title: Montel's theorem and tautness in calibrated geometry
item.description: arXiv:2606.31393v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We relate the hyperbolicity of a calibrated manifold $(X, \phi)$ to the analytic properties of the space of Smith immersions $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ from the Poincare $k$-ball into $X$. In particular, we establish the following calibrated analogue of a theorem of Royden: if $X$ is $\phi$-saturated, then $R_\phi$- and $K_\phi$-hyperbolicity coincide, and either implies the equicontinuity of $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ with respect to the $\phi$-distance. This yields a Montel theorem for compact $\phi$-saturated calibrated manifolds as an immediate corollary. Our primary technical tool is a new Schwarz lemma for Smith immersions from $B^k$ into $X$, which is of independent interest. In a similar spirit, we also prove a calibrated analogue of Kiernan's theorem to the effect that the $K_\phi$-hyperbolicity of $X$ is almost equivalent to $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ being a normal family. Finally, we prove that bounded domains in flat euclidean space are $R_\phi$-hyperbolic for any calibration $\phi$, and we investigate the hyperbolicity of products and discrete quotients.
item.dc:creator: Anton Iliashenko, Spiro Karigiannis, Jesse Madnick

item.title: Degeneracies of Lagrange functions and geometric interpretations of Lagrange multipliers
item.description: arXiv:2608.19517v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce Lagrange functions associated with height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves. We show that degeneracies of these functions characterize geometric properties of the curves, such as inflections and vertices, and give geometric interpretations of the corresponding Lagrange multipliers in terms of contact with lines and circles.
item.dc:creator: Masaru Hasegawa

item.title: A proof of the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture for small volumes under a Ricci curvature lower bound
item.description: arXiv:2609.17093v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, also known as the Aubin conjecture, in the small volume regime under a lower Ricci curvature bound, for any dimension $n\geq 2$. More precisely, we show that if $(M^n,g)$ is a Cartan-Hadamard manifold satisfying $\mathrm{Sec}_g\leq\bar k\leq 0$ and $\mathrm{Ric}_g\geq (n-1)\underline k$, then its isoperimetric profile is at least that of the model space of curvature $\bar k$ for small enough volumes. We also reduce the proof of the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture to establishing rigidity in the equality case.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Agnoletto, M\'arcio Fabiano Da Silva, Stefano Nardulli, Reinaldo Resende

item.title: Minimal Products via Weighted Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2609.24886v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an exact composition principle for spherical immersions coupled through coefficient profiles and norm-preserving bilinear maps. Under explicit mixed orthogonality, the spherical mean curvature vector splits into orthogonal input and profile contributions. The composition is minimal if and only if every input is minimal and the profile is $W$-minimal for the induced monomial weight. Tensor iteration allows weighted profiles to serve as inputs in further compositions. At fixed weights, Hsiang--Lawson reduction and Kapouleas--McGrath doubling yield closed embedded $W$-minimal profiles. When the effective exponents tend to infinity in positive limiting proportions, Gaussian transfer produces interior coefficient profiles from closed embedded self-shrinkers that are nondegenerate modulo rotations. The number of distinct corresponding profiles is bounded below by the Lusternik--Schnirelmann category of the rotation orbit.
item.dc:creator: Yongsheng Zhang

item.title: A gluing construction of $Z$-extremal K\"ahler metrics and new examples of Bismut Hermitian-Einstein $3$-folds
item.description: arXiv:2609.25250v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a gluing construction for a class of 6th order geometric non-linear PDE's on a K\"ahler manifold or orbifold, arising in the study of Bismut Hermitian Einstein complex $3$-folds, the supersymmetric supergravity models in physics, and in Dervan's Z-critical K\"ahler metrics. As applications, we obtain a desingularization theorem for orbifolds with crepant singularities admitting a solution of the PDE, as well as a blowing-up of points theorem for smooth complex $3$-folds admitting such solutions. These results yield new examples of regular Bismut Hermitian Einstein structures on the smooth manifolds $3(S^2\times S^4)\sharp 4(S^3\times S^3)$, $5(S^2\times S^4)\sharp 6(S^3\times S^3)$ and $S^1\times 9(S^2\times S^3)$, as well as infinite topological types of smooth compact $7$-dimensional manifolds $Y_7$, providing new solutions to the supersymmetric ${\rm AdS}_3 \times Y_7$ type IIB and ${\rm AdS}_2 \times T^2 \times Y^7$ type $D=11$ supergravity models.
item.dc:creator: Vestislav Apostolov, Abdellah Lahdili, Kuan-Hui Lee, Fr\'ed\'eric Rochon

item.title: A short proof of Bernstein's theorem via the Omori--Yau maximum principle
item.description: arXiv:2609.33643v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a short, self-contained proof of Bernstein's theorem: every entire minimal graph in $R^3$ is a plane. The only global tool is the Omori-Yau maximum principle, which holds on entire minimal graphs with their induced metric. We apply it exactly once to a single explicit function $F$ built from the surface's angle function and principal curvatures. A pointwise differential inequality for $F$, combined with the Omori-Yau principle, forces it to attain its minimum value everywhere, which yields the planarity of the surface and hence Bernstein's theorem. As a by-product of our approach, we show that the same method, with a different function and with some extra work, also proves in a simple and self-contained way the generalization of Bernstein's theorem given by Osserman that a complete minimal surface in $R^3$ whose normals omit a neighbourhood of some direction must be a plane.
item.dc:creator: Luis J. Alias, Miguel A. Mero\~no

item.title: Scalar curvature bounds and tangent cones for K\"ahler--Ricci shrinkers
item.description: arXiv:2610.05643v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a uniform scalar curvature bound, depending only on the dimension, for K\"ahler--Ricci shrinkers. We also prove that every noncompact K\"ahler--Ricci shrinker has a unique tangent cone at infinity, naturally homeomorphic to the base of its polarized Fano fibration. For shrinkers with maximal volume growth, this cone is isometric to the metric completion of the regular part equipped with the intrinsic distance induced by the limiting K\"ahler metric.
item.dc:creator: Yu Li, Junsheng Zhang

item.title: A Converse to the Archimedes Sphere Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.06261v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that a convex surface in Euclidean 3-space is a sphere if the area cut off from it by a slab of some fixed width depends only on the direction of the slab. This result generalizes theorems of Blaschke and Stamm, which assumed the slab-area property for every width. It holds also for any smooth closed embedded surface, and we obtain analogous results in higher dimensions. The proof is based on an averaging identity, which relates slab areas to the Newtonian potential of the surface, the electrostatic characterization of spheres by Mendez and Reichel, and analytic microlocal properties of the Radon transform, which are used to show that the slab-area property forces real analyticity, via theorems of Kashiwara and Boman.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Ghomi, Ralph Howard, Mijia Lai

item.title: Modified support measures and Alexandrov-Fenchel type inequalities for nonsmooth h-convex bodies in hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2610.18761v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and its modified version for arbitrary, possibly nonsmooth, horospherically convex bodies in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}, n\geq 2$, and prove that equality in each inequality holds if and only if the h-convex body is a geodesic ball. A key ingredient is a rigidity theorem characterizing geodesic balls via proportionality between modified support measures of adjacent orders. Its proof combines the $C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,k+1}$ approximation of the outer parallel hypersurfaces by smooth strictly h-convex hypersurfaces with the estimates for the total variation norm of the signed measure associated with the proportionality relation along the shifted curvature flows independent of initial curvature bounds. For $0\leq k\leq n-1$, we construct weak flows preserving the $k$-th modified quermassintegral $\tilde{W}_k$ with arbitrary h-convex initial bodies as Hausdorff limits of the smooth flows. The rigidity theorem above characterizes the limit shape of the flow and gives a positive lower bound on the rate of decrease of $\tilde{W}_{k+1}$ for a short time whenever the initial h-convex body is not a geodesic ball, which characterizes the equality cases in the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality. For the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we establish the Hausdorff stability independent of curvature bounds described by the Alexandrov-Fenchel deficits for h-convex bodies, which characterizes the equality cases in the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality.
item.dc:creator: Xinxiu Zhang

item.title: Observing minimal submanifolds with isolated singularities on open sets of metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22229v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a perturbative theory for minimal submanifolds with only (strongly) isolated singularities, with respect to varying background Riemannian metrics. As an application, we obtain a general "sporadic persistence" criterion, thus naturally complementing the non-persistence theorem by the authors. In particular, such a criterion is satisfied by the spherical suspension in $\mathbb{S}^{3m+2}$ of the Veronese embedding of $\mathbb{K}\mathbb{P}^2$ for $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H},\mathbb{O}$ (the normed division algebras) in the round spheres of dimension $3m+1=4,7,13,25$ respectively, thereby providing families of continuously varying $(2m+1)$-dimensional stationary varifolds with isolated singularities that are observable on an open set of metrics. By our previous results, these phenomena cannot possibly occur in the codimension one scenario.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Carlotto, Yangyang Li, Zhihan Wang

item.title: A complete K\"ahler metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ of nonnegative Ricci curvature with Euclidean volume growth and nonunique asymptotic cone
item.description: arXiv:2610.32734v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct complete smooth K\"ahler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^n$ , $n\ge2$, with nonnegative Ricci curvature, Euclidean volume growth, and nonunique tangent cones at infinity. More generally, we prescribe the entire tangent cone set within a class of smooth Hopf cones, using a compact connected family of positive transverse Ricci forms on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We identify all metric blow-downs and their Ricci currents, compute the exact asymptotic volume ratio, and classify isometries between the model cones. In particular, the K\"ahler condition does not ensure uniqueness at infinity under nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, even in complex dimension two.
